candidate_metadata_split: The tested candidate source/artifact is immutable before proof generation. Proof metadata may be committed or stored later, but must bind back to the unchanged candidate subject.

assertions: penta_id and stable institutional identity are unchanged
provider, host, process and model identifiers do not replace institutional identity
identity proof resolves to the declared registry record
cases.fault: terminate the process and start the exact artifact on a new process identity

assertions: authoritative state is recovered without model inference
schema and checkpoint versions match the contract
RPO and RTO remain within declared limits
cases.fault: clear all process memory and restart from the declared authoritative store

assertions: each deterministic function returns the recorded output digest
side effects are isolated behind the deterministic execution boundary
compiled behavior hash and function-set hash match the contract
cases.fault: replay stored inputs with the model disabled

assertions: the same idempotency key is reused
no duplicate authoritative effect or receipt is created
retry and dead-letter behavior match declared policy
cases.fault: crash after dequeue and redeliver the same stable job ID

assertions: the new owner receives a higher fencing token
the stale owner is denied after expiry
conflicting ownership cannot produce duplicate effects
cases.fault: stop lease renewal, allow TTL expiry and start a replacement owner

assertions: PentaDND preserves active leases, TTLs and conflict precedence
expired restrictions release only through deterministic clock and policy logic
model absence cannot bypass, extend or invent a restriction
cases.fault: remove model access during overlapping do-not-disturb leases and TTL expiry

assertions: queued, leased, completed, failed and dead-letter states survive
stable work IDs and ownership history remain queryable
no work is silently dropped or duplicated
cases.fault: restart all workers with the model unavailable

assertions: assignment and accountable-owner records persist
orphaned work is deterministically reconciled
model output cannot reassign accountable ownership
cases.fault: restart the project/work owner runtime during active assignments

assertions: append-only evidence history remains complete and ordered
receipt hashes and subject bindings remain valid
rejected actions are not rewritten as successful
cases.fault: restart the Penta after accepted and rejected actions exist

assertions: authority is re-resolved from CHLOM and accountable-owner records
missing, expired or mismatched authority fails closed
model availability does not alter the authority result
cases.fault: disable the model and restart before a consequential mutation

assertions: certificate subject must match the exact source and artifact
candidate SHA, certified SHA and production SHA must remain equal
mismatched or stale certificate causes HOLD_FAIL_CLOSED
cases.fault: replace source or artifact after certification and attempt release

assertions: case identity and state persist
stored inputs replay to the same deterministic disposition
model replacement cannot rewrite prior case outcomes
cases.fault: restart between case intake, deterministic evaluation and evidence preservation

assertions: the exact phase cursor and completed dependency set persist
the next run resumes from durable state rather than chat memory
already completed effects are not repeated
cases.fault: restart during a multi-phase convergence run

assertions: the declared degraded mode is entered
identity, state, authority, queue and lease safety remain intact
allowed and forbidden operations match the contract
health distinguishes model degradation from deterministic-core failure
persistent identity and state are unchanged
authority results and deterministic replay results are unchanged
provider/model identity does not become Penta identity
incompatible model output is rejected or held
cases.fault: replace the model/provider through the declared adapter contract

assertions: each boundary converges to one authoritative outcome
outbox, execution, receipt and audit remain reconcilable
no boundary creates a duplicate effect or missing terminal evidence
cases.fault: inject crashes before commit, after commit before outbox, after outbox before execution, and after execution before receipt

assertions: the restored state digest matches the declared recovery point
the Penta can perform deterministic health and replay checks in isolation
no provider write or production promotion occurs during recovery proof
cases.fault: restore into an isolated environment with the model disabled

completion_rule: A production Penta passes only when every applicable case has immutable exact-subject evidence, the contract validates, the evidence is unexpired, and an independent verifier attests the bundle. Missing or failed cases remain HOLD_FAIL_CLOSED.
execution_rule: Every case must run against the exact source commit, artifact SHA-256, doctrine version and compiled behavior hash declared by the subject PENTA_SURVIVAL_CONTRACT. A plan is not evidence until immutable receipts are attached.
global_invariants: persistent identity remains the same across process and node replacement
authoritative state rehydrates from durable external storage
candidate SHA equals certified SHA equals production SHA
model output is never an authority source
no duplicate authoritative effects or receipts are created
queue job IDs and idempotency keys remain stable
CHLOM authority and DAIL history remain intact
health reports model loss separately from deterministic-core failure
global_preconditions: The exact candidate artifact and source commit are pinned.
The model adapter is disabled or disconnected without disabling the deterministic runtime.
Authoritative state, queues, lease stores, CHLOM authority records, DAIL evidence and health telemetry are available through their declared recovery paths.
No test may manufacture provider readback, certification, authority, receipts or production state.
purpose: Prove that each Penta's deterministic authority and continuity survive model removal, process restart, node replacement, redelivery, lease loss and exact-release recovery.
